title: Face with Crossed-Out Eyes Emoji 😵 Meaning: Knocked Out
description: The face with crossed-out eyes emoji 😵 has X-shaped eyes: shocked, knocked out, wiped out or figuratively dead. See how it differs from the spiral-eyed 😵‍💫.
summary: The 😵 face with crossed-out eyes means knocked out. People use it when they are stunned by news, flattened by exhaustion, overwhelmed by a workload or, as an exaggeration, dead from laughter or embarrassment. It was long known as the dizzy face, and some still use it for dizziness.
meaning: Xs for eyes are the comic-strip mark of a character who has been knocked unconscious or killed, and that is the image here. 😵 says something hit the sender hard. It might be a piece of shocking gossip, a brutal exam, a price tag or a day so long that they collapsed the moment they got home.

The emoji's history explains its mixed use. For years its common name was dizzy face, and some platforms drew it with swirls instead of Xs. When a separate face with spiral eyes was introduced, this one was renamed to describe what most vendors actually showed: crossed-out eyes. Many people still pick it for vertigo or confusion out of habit.

In current usage the knocked-out meanings dominate. It appears for hangovers, for shock in the sense of I can't believe what I just read, and for being overwhelmed, as when a to-do list has defeated you. It is close in spirit to the skull emoji's I'm dead, but with more surprise and less laughter.

It also has a literal place in talk about fights, falls and fainting. Boxing and wrestling fans use it for a knockout, gamers for an eliminated character, and it sometimes marks something as lethal, such as a hot sauce or a workout. The face itself is cartoonish, so it rarely feels morbid.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It works as a compact reaction to overwhelming information. A friend sends the cost of their car repair and you answer 😵. It also describes your own state after a double shift or a long drive. A single one is usually enough; it already implies you have nothing left to add.

contexts.label: In gaming and sports
contexts.body: Players use it when their character is taken out, when they lose badly or when an opponent pulls off something they did not see coming. In combat sports it marks a knockout. It is a common shorthand in kill feeds and stream chats for getting eliminated.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It reacts to jaw-dropping reveals, plot twists and prices. Fitness creators caption punishing workouts with it. It is used less for laughter than 💀 or 😭, so in comment sections it tends to signal real shock or exhaustion rather than amusement.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Among colleagues it is a relatable way to say your inbox, calendar or week has flattened you. It is informal but not offensive. Avoid it in reply to a specific request, where it can look like you are complaining about the person asking.

examples.meaning: The sender is stunned by bad financial news.
The workout was intense enough to finish them off.

combos.meaning: Seeing stars after a hit or a shock; on older devices this is also how the spiral-eyes emoji appears.
Knocked out, literally in a fight or figuratively by events.
Destroyed by a night of drinking.
Flattened by studying or an exam.

confusedWith.difference: 😵‍💫 has hypnotic swirls for eyes and means dizzy, disoriented or confused. 😵 has Xs and means knocked out or stunned. The first is still spinning; the second has already hit the floor.
💀 says I'm dead mostly from laughter or secondhand embarrassment and is the favorite of younger users. 😵 covers shock and exhaustion, and is seldom used to say something was funny.
😲 is wide-eyed and gasping, still upright and taking the news in. 😵 has gone past surprise to collapse. Use 😲 for wow and 😵 for that finished me.

avoid: Do not use it in conversations about a real death, overdose or serious accident.
Avoid it when describing someone else as passed out drunk in a public post.
If you are truly faint or unwell, say so in words instead of relying on a cartoon face.
design: A yellow face with two X marks in place of eyes and a round, open mouth. Current designs from the major vendors all use the Xs. Before the spiral-eyed emoji existed, some platforms showed this character with swirling eyes instead, which is why older screenshots and descriptions call it the dizzy face.

faqs.a: That the sender is stunned, overwhelmed or worn out to the point of collapse. It is an exaggeration in nearly every case. Read it as I can't handle this, said about news, work, a workout or a hangover.

It can stand for figuratively dead, since X eyes are a cartoon sign for it. In practice most people use the skull 💀 for that joke. 😵 leans toward shocked or knocked out, and is a less common choice for dying of laughter.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😵 and 😵‍💫?
faqs.a: The newer 😵‍💫 was created specifically for dizziness and has spiral eyes. 😵 kept the X eyes and the knocked-out sense. Technically the spiral version is built from 😵 joined with the dizzy symbol 💫, so the two are related under the hood.

faqs.q: Why did the dizzy face emoji change?
faqs.a: It did not so much change as get clarified. Vendors had drawn it inconsistently, some with Xs and some with spirals. Adding a dedicated spiral-eyes emoji let this one settle on crossed-out eyes, and its descriptive name was updated to match.
